Figure 1: Schematic of visual processing and neural responses. Left: topographic mapping of visual stimuli in the retina and visual cortex, with panels (a) and (b) reproducing classic studies [9]. Due to greater cortical resources allocated to foveal input, perception exhibits a fovea-centered blur, differing from the original stimulus. Right: staged neural processing of visual understanding, sequentially involving background-related diffuse activity, low-level feature extraction in the posterior occipital cortex, perceptual organization in the occipitotemporal pathway, and high-level semantic representation in occipital regions, with each stage corresponding to distinct brain activations and visual representations.

Figure 2: Overall framework of MB2L.(1) Adaptive Blur with Visual Priors (top-left): The original image undergoes biomimetic blurring, then hierarchical visual features are extracted via low- and high-level encoders; (2) Biomimetic Visual Feature Extraction (bottom-left): EEG signals are split by a channel-weighted layer, then encoded into hierarchical features through cross-attention; (3) Multi-level Bidirectional Contrastive Learning (right): Cross-modal features are projected and aligned via contrastive loss, enabling zero-shot retrieval and classification.
